title.narrative: Output 6.2. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen policies and strategies to promote and ensure equal opportunities, participation and treatment between women and men, including equal remuneration for work of equal value

description.narrative:
In May 2023, the national constituents of Uzbekistan and the Republican Commission on Enhancing the Role of Women in Society, Gender Equality and Family adopted a tripartite statement called ‘’Communique on promoting gender equality and decent work in Uzbekistan’’ as a final outcome of the ILO High-Level Conference on Pathways to Gender Equality and Decent Work in Uzbekistan held on 23 May 2023 in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. At the conclusion of the Conference, all participants reaffirmed their unwavering commitment to upholding the principles of equality between women and men and the elimination of discrimination in employment. Together, they reached a consensus on the following provisions to guide their collective efforts as part of the Communique: 1. recognizes that gender equality and women's empowerment are one of the most important factors for sustainable development and inclusive economic growth, 2. addresses prevalence of gender gaps and inequalities in the world of work which requires identifying the root causes of inequality and tackle multiple interconnected forms of discrimination to create a comprehensive agenda for gender equality, 3. highlights the need to ensure adequate, timely and high-quality policies to protect women and men from disadvantaged groups, especially in terms of full access to decent employment opportunities and social protection, through inclusive policies and targeted counteraction to various forms of discrimination, 4. underlines the importance of a culture change in society to ensure gender equality and non-discrimination, 5. outlines the need for inclusive macroeconomic policies that promote the transition from the informal to the formal economy and 6. calls for the ratification of ILO Conventions 183 on maternity protection and Convention 102 on social security. Within the framework of the RBSA project on Supporting development of gender responsive policies and programmes on care economy and decent work for care workers in Uzbekistan, ILO organised a High-Level Conference on Pathways to Gender Equality and Decent Work in Uzbekistan held on 23 May 2023 in Tashkent with participation of the Chairperson of the Senate/Head of the Committee on Women and Gender Equality of the Senate, the Minister of Employment and Poverty Reduction, the Chairpersons of Federation of Trade Unions of Uzbekistan and Confederation of Employers of Uzbekistan. Representatives of UN Agencies, IFIs, NGOs and academia were present at the conference.
The High-Level Conference aimed to reaffirm the commitment of the tripartite constituents to implementing the ILO's transformative agenda on gender equality and decent work. The conference served as a forum to share knowledge on reducing structural decent work deficits and inequalities through comprehensive policies, underpinned by principles of social dialogue. As a result of the Conference and considering the main discussion points at the conference by the presenters, the national tripartite statement (the Communique) on gender equality. The ILO provided technical guidance in drafting of the Communique where ILO’s priority areas regarding promoting gender equality and social justice in Uzbekistan were reflected.
The ILO provided technical support through providing guidance throughout the tripartite discussions on the General Collective Agreement process.

description.narrative:
In November 2022, the Government of Uzbekistan together with other member states of UNESCO (The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) has adopted the Tashkent Declaration Commitments to Action for Transforming Early Childhood Care and Education at the at the World Conference on Early Childhood Care and Education.
The Tashkent Declaration is intended to set the international agenda for early childhood education and establishes a set of guiding principles to build a global strategy for early childhood care and education (ECCE) system: improving the quality and relevance of curricula and pedagogy; ensuring equal and inclusive educational services for all children and protecting and guaranteeing the rights to access ECCE in emergency situations. The Declaration clearly addresses ILO’s decent work agenda by integrating a rights-based approach including wages and working conditions of care workers (ECCE personnel) and recognizing the core labour rights and social dialogue. In response to the request of UNESCO, ILO provided technical inputs during the drafting process of the Declaration with a view to integrate ILO’s decent work agenda and 5R Framework for Decent Care Work. The final version of the Declaration reflects ILO’s inputs highlighting the need for improving working conditions and wages of the ECCE personnel. Further, the Declaration underlines that promoting the organization and representation of ECCE personnel as well as their right to social dialogue and collective bargaining can play an important role in promoting decent work for ECCE personnel.
As the signatory of the Declaration, the member states of UNESCO including Uzbekistan, committed to strengthen ECCE systems including the recruitment, qualifications and working conditions of all ECCE personnel and improve regulatory and quality assurance frameworks, striving towards policies and interventions on equal qualifications, certifications, wages and status between ECCE and, at least, primary school teachers.
ILO continues to support the constituents through technical discussion on ILO’s agenda on care economy and care work. Within the framework of the RBSA project on care economy, a tripartite dialogue was organised on 12 July 2023 to introduce Global tool on Care Investment Simulator with participation of the Ministry of Employment and Poverty Reduction, workers’ and employers’ organisations. In July 2023, ILO has initiated collection of national data to populate the investment simulator to develop a report on care work and policy recommendations to promote care policies for workers with family responsibilities.
